faq.ricerca: statute of limitations meaning
faq.q: What does statute of limitations mean?
faq.a: It is the deadline, set by law, for starting a lawsuit. The federal debt collection rule defines it as the period prescribed by applicable law for bringing a legal action. Each state sets its own periods for each kind of claim, and rules on minors, absence from the state or late discovery can move the date.

faq.ricerca: statute of repose vs statute of limitations
faq.q: What is the difference between a statute of repose and a statute of limitations?
faq.a: A statute of limitations usually runs from when a claim accrues and can be paused. A statute of repose is an outer limit counted from the act itself. Texas, for example, gives health care claims {P:TX/medical-malpractice:0} under {CIT:TX/medical-malpractice:0} and adds a 10-year cut-off that the statute calls a statute of repose, so that all claims must be brought within 10 years.

faq.ricerca: tolling statute of limitations meaning
faq.q: What does tolling the statute of limitations mean?
faq.a: Tolling means the clock stops for a while. For example, Texas does not count the time the person being sued is absent from the state, and Washington does not count the time the person with the claim is under 18 when it accrues. Each state lists its own tolling rules, and they have conditions.

faq.ricerca: statute of limitations calculator
faq.q: How does this statute of limitations calculator work?
faq.a: Choose a state, a type of claim and the date to count from. The calculator adds the general period written in the statute and shows the date, plus any outer limit. It does not apply tolling or exceptions, does not move weekend dates and is not legal advice: it lists the exceptions so you can ask a licensed attorney.

faq.ricerca: statute of limitations for minors
faq.q: Does the statute of limitations run against minors?
faq.a: In general, many states pause or delay the deadline while the person with the claim is under 18: Texas does not count the time of the disability, and Ohio lets the claim be brought after the disability is removed. Medical malpractice often has its own shorter rules for children: in Texas a child injured before age 12 has until the 14th birthday.

faq.ricerca: can a debt collector sue after statute of limitations
faq.q: Can a debt collector sue after the statute of limitations?
faq.a: Under the federal Regulation F, a debt collector must not bring or threaten to bring a legal action against a consumer to collect a time-barred debt, meaning a debt for which the applicable statute of limitations has expired. Which period applies, and whether it has expired, depends on state law and the facts.

faq.ricerca: time barred debt meaning
faq.q: What is a time-barred debt?
faq.a: The federal rule defines a time-barred debt as a debt for which the applicable statute of limitations has expired. The debt may still exist, but a debt collector must not sue or threaten to sue the consumer over it.
